record.paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
record.context_brief: Rate-privacy tradeoff for PRUW with sparsification
record.original_question: For PRUW in private federated learning or federated submodel learning with sparsification, how does the communication cost change if the privacy requirement is relaxed through a rate-privacy tradeoff, for example by incorporating differential privacy so that a specified amount of information may leak about the desired indices and the values of selected updates or parameters, rather than only about sparse-update indices as in existing rate-privacy-storage tradeoff work?

evidence.quote: In FL with top r sparsification, clients only download and upload the most significant r′ and r fractions of parameters and updates, respectively, to reduce the communication cost.

Motivated by these privacy concerns, the problem of PRUW in FL with top r sparsification is introduced in [26], [47], [48]. The privacy constraint on the downloaded (uploaded) parameter (update) indices requires the mutual information between the real indices and all the information received by an individual database to be equal to zero.

The rate-privacy-storage trade off in [48] only allows information to be leaked on the indices of the sparse updates in FL with sparsification, which does not have a significant impact on the communication rate. An interesting direction is to investigate the rate-privacy trade off in PRUW by incorporating differential privacy as in [4], [14] to see the effect on the communication cost in private FSL/FL with sparsification when allowing a given amount of information to be leaked on the desired indices as well as the values of the selected updates/parameters.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of Private Read–Update–Write (PRUW) in federated learning / federated submodel learning with top-r sparsification, defined as follows. A model consisting of M submodels is stored, in a coded fashion, across N non-colluding databases. In each round, a client (i) downloads (reads) a fraction r' of the parameters of one desired submodel — the "most significant" parameters according to a sparsification rule — and (ii) uploads (writes) updates to a fraction r of the parameters of that submodel. Communication cost is measured by the read rate R_R = L/D and write rate R_W = L/U, where L is the number of symbols of useful information, and D, U are the total numbers of symbols downloaded and uploaded per round, respectively.

In the standard information-theoretic privacy formulation, the mutual information between (a) the index of the desired submodel, (b) the indices (positions) of the sparse parameters/updates, and (c) the values of those updates, on one side, and all information observed by any individual database, on the other side, is required to be exactly zero. Existing rate–privacy–storage tradeoffs only relax the zero-leakage requirement on the indices of the sparse updates, which has limited impact on the communication rate.

Problem: Formulate and characterize the rate–privacy tradeoff for PRUW with top-r sparsification when privacy is relaxed via a differential-privacy-style constraint that simultaneously permits a prescribed amount of information leakage about (1) the index of the desired submodel, (2) the indices of the selected sparse parameters/updates, and (3) the values of the selected updates/parameters. Specifically, determine the optimal achievable read and write communication rates (R_R, R_W) as functions of the allowed leakage parameters (e.g., (ε, δ)-DP budgets or analogous mutual-information bounds) for each of the three categories of information, and exhibit explicit schemes attaining these rates.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing work on PRUW with sparsification addresses information-theoretic privacy and a rate–distortion or rate–privacy–storage tradeoff that allows leakage only on the indices of sparse updates. No published result was found that characterizes the rate–privacy tradeoff under a differential-privacy-style relaxation permitting leakage on the desired submodel index and the values of selected updates/parameters; this is posed as a future research direction and appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Private Read Update Write (PRUW) in FSL: Communication Efficient Schemes With and Without Sparsification
status_evidence.snippet: Sparsification scheme guarantees information-theoretic privacy of the updating submodel index, values of sparse updates and positions of sparse updates/parameters.
status_evidence.claim: Existing PRUW-with-sparsification schemes enforce strict information-theoretic privacy on indices and values, not a DP relaxation.

status_evidence.title: Rate Distortion Tradeoff in Private Read Update Write in Federated Submodel Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Linear rate-distortion relation is achievable while guaranteeing information-theoretic privacy of the updating submodel index and the values of updates.
status_evidence.claim: Known tradeoff studies use distortion or limited index-leakage, not a DP-style leakage budget on values and desired indices.
